etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English purifien, purifyen, from Old French purifier, purifiier, from Latin pūrificō, pūrificāre, from pūrus (“pure; clean”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cleanse, or rid of impurities.

quote.citation: 2020 May 4, “Young Practitioners Should Carefully Read “How the Specter of Communism Is Ruling Our World””, in Minghui‎[1]:
quote.text: The modern arts deviate from the standards set forth by the divine—art should be used to purify one’s heart and improve one’s morality.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To free from guilt or sin.
